description: Steve Fezzik review, checked 20 Nov 2026: SIC Picks prices, contest wins checked on official standings, his 2026 SuperContest entries, and buyer posts since 2009.
dek: A two time SuperContest champion who left Pregame.com in 2026 and now sells NFL and college football picks through SIC Picks, from $79 a week to $1,199 a season. Several of his contest finishes are on the organizers' own standings, including a 2025 win. His paid pick record is not public, his unit totals differ from page to page, and buyers have argued about his paid results since 2009.

short_answer: Steve Fezzik is a real, well known Las Vegas bettor. The Las Vegas Sun reported in January 2010 that he won the Las Vegas Hilton Supercontest two years in a row, and official 2025 standings we opened show an entry under the alias FEZZIK-1 winning the Westgate SuperContest second half contest and an entry FEZZIK-3 tied for 9th in the Circa Sports Million. In that sense he is legitimate.

Contest results are not the same product as the picks he sells, and the full contest picture is more modest than the headline. Across all five of his 2025 Circa entries the combined record was 244-197-9, about 55%, not the 64% of the entry he advertises. In the 2026 Westgate SuperContest, after Week 10 his two entries stood at 18-31-1 and 24-26, tied 570th and 327th of 596 entries.

His paid picks at SIC Picks sit behind a login. The unit totals in his marketing (+215, +241, +257 and +500 units over various spans) come from him or his sellers and do not agree with each other. Buyers have argued about his paid results since a 2009 tracker put his forum plays at minus 30.77 units.

Treat Fezzik as a proven contest player whose paid record is unproven for today's buyer. If you buy, buy a week first, log every pick with the line and time you received it, and judge it over a full season or more.

guarantee: We found no guarantee on any Steve Fezzik package. Each package lists what is included: futures, sides, totals, props, and email and SMS pick alerts. The SIC FAQ says: "Purchases are non-refundable unless a specific promotion, guarantee, or written policy states otherwise."

The packages are shown as priced "/ yearly" or "/ weekly". The SIC terms say paid services are "typically offered in annual increments or by a specific sporting period season", that SIC may "increase a Service's fees or institute new charges at any time", and allow automatic card payments if you choose them. We did not find clear wording on whether a weekly package renews on its own, so check your account settings after you buy. The terms are governed by California law.

The SIC FAQ also advises judging results "over a meaningful sample, at least one month" and recommends line shopping because small differences in odds affect long term results. Both points are sound. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: How we checked the units: his own website lists yearly totals of +64, +32, +100, +42 and +19 for 2020 to 2024, which add to 257. His Pregame bio gives +241 for the same five years, and in a January 2026 forum reply he wrote "just under 260 UNITS". The SIC page gives +215 for 2020 to 2026. If the 257 is right, the 215 implies he lost about 42 units across 2025 and 2026 so far, a figure none of his pages states. A Pregame forum member claimed a 95 unit loss for 2025 alone. None of these totals comes with a public log, a unit size or the prices taken.

How we checked the contests: we opened the organizers' PDFs. The Circa Sports standings list five FEZZIK entries in the 2025 Million: one tied for 9th at 56-31-3, and the others at 50-38-2 (tied 308th), 50-39-1 (tied 379th), 47-42-1 (tied 1,035th) and 41-47-2 (tied 3,310th). Added together that is 244-197-9, 55.3%. The Westgate 2025 half season contests list FEZZIK-1 first at 34-10-1 and FEZZIK-2 tied for 79th at 26-18-1 in the second half, and 18-27 and 20-25 in the first half; all four together come to 98-80-2, 55.1%. That is a winning rate against contest lines, but well below the best entry he quotes.

The 2026 season so far: Westgate's full season standings after Week 10 list 596 entries. FEZZIK-1 was tied for 570th at 18-31-1 and FEZZIK-2 tied for 327th at 24-26, a combined 42-57-1. Its Weeks 1 to 9 contest, already final, had them tied 503rd and 270th. We do not know for certain that these aliases are his, but they match the ones in his 2025 claims. His SIC page does not mention 2026 contest results.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: contest results published by the organizers. We opened the Westgate 2025 SuperContest standings, which show FEZZIK-1 first in the Weeks 10 to 18 contest at 34-10-1 with a $50,000 prize, and the Circa Sports Million VII full season standings, which show FEZZIK-3 tied for 9th at 56-31-3 with a $70,000 prize. The standings list aliases, not legal names, but the aliases and results match what Fezzik advertises. The Las Vegas Sun reported on 16 Jan 2010 that he won the 2009 Hilton Supercontest at 52-29-3 for $196,800, after cashing for $210,000 the year before, and called it the first back to back title in the contest's 20 year history. We did not open organizer standings for 2008 or 2009.

Those contests are a different product from the paid picks. Contest entries are five NFL sides a week against fixed lines; the packages at SIC Picks include futures, totals and props at market prices. A strong contest finish does not tell you how the paid picks did. As one Sportsbook Review member put it in 2010, winning a contest takes a very different approach from picking winners against real lines.

What the seller side publishes: the SIC FAQ says results are "updated daily and available on the website", but the link goes to a picks dashboard that asks you to sign in, and we found no public log of Fezzik's SIC picks. An undated update on his SIC page claimed "CFB 8-0-1 & NFL 8-4 for +22 units". Pregame.com still shows a profile and archive of his Pregame picks, last seen by us with picks dated to 5 Apr 2026. That archive was graded by the company that sold his picks, and we did not total it. In 2015 Pregame announced that a tracker would log his Bet Like a Pro program in a forum thread; we opened only the first page of that thread and make no claim about its totals.

Earlier tracking by buyers: when he posted plays on a paid Las Vegas Advisor forum, members kept their own counts. One member counted him 71-49 weighted in October 2009. In December 2009 another shared a tally of 127-142.5-3, minus 30.77 units, for college and NFL plays; the site's administrator replied that he did not know how accurate it was and that he had made money on the picks. In January 2010 a member listed his football futures as 16-4, and others replied that some losing futures and bowl totals were left out. These are buyer counts, not audits.

Background: a Los Angeles Times profile from 2006, reposted in full on TheRX, said Fezzik is a pen name, that he grew up in Dayton, Ohio, graduated from Northwestern in 1986, became an actuary and rose to vice president at Transamerica Asset Management before moving to Las Vegas in 2001, and that he gave the paper his real name so his story could be confirmed. It also said he then wagered about $60,000 a day with a small crew of partners.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Steve Fezzik runs from 2009 to 2026 and sits mostly on forums: the Las Vegas Advisor forum where he once posted paid plays, Sportsbook Review, TheRX, Reddit and Pregame's own forum. We found no reviews of his new SIC Picks packages. Below is what we read and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We read about 15 independent posts from 2009 to 2026. The same split runs through all of them: respect for Fezzik as a sharp bettor and contest player, and doubt about his paid or posted picks. On the paid Las Vegas Advisor forum in 2009 and 2012, some members thanked him for winning futures and totals while others tallied his posted plays as losing and said they joined only for his picks; in 2010 a former subscriber on Sportsbook Review said they lost money following him and that critical posts and record tallies were removed. In 2024 and 2026, members of Pregame's forum alleged a losing 2024 NFL season, plays on both sides of one game, and a 95 unit loss in 2025, while others defended him as a proven winner who cares. In 2025 a TheRX member's running count had his paid picks down about 73 units by mid August, a Reddit commenter said he had been in the red for two years, and TheRX members warned that a site using his name was fake. No post includes a full log, and we could not verify any figure.

A Pregame forum member posted that Fezzik "lost -95 Units for his clients in 2025" and gave no log. Fezzik replied that he won just under 260 units from 2020 to 2024 and told readers to buy another handicapper rather than him. The next day another member argued that no buyer won those units once fees and lines buyers could not get are counted. We did not verify any of these figures.
In the same thread several members defended him. One wrote that unhappy buyers at least know he has a winning track record and that he cares, judging by his reply.

A member alleged that Fezzik sent paying clients the Rams +3 while saying on a podcast that the Rams had no chance against the 49ers, and cited a 2024 paid NFL record of 62-58-2 without a source. Another member who said they had followed many paid handicappers for ten years called him irrelevant apart from one streak. We could not check either claim.

Fezzik posted that he would stop providing services to Pregame after the NCAA basketball games, ending about 13 years there. Members wished him well; one called him sharp in nearly everything he does. A video posted by Sports Injury Central announced that he was joining SICPicks.com.

In an r/sportsbook thread about paying for picks, a commenter who said they bet full time and once worked for an odds provider told readers never to pay for picks, and wrote that Fezzik and another well known seller had been in the red for their services for the last two years. No figures were posted.

In a TheRX service play thread, a member who reposts paid plays listed three of his college football plays with a running tally of "2025 YTD down 72.76 units" after 17 Aug 2025 and a 2024 college football line of 84-75-6, 52.8%. Days later the same member wrote that Fezzik's CFL plays were often copies of another Pregame pro's, at 8-9. These are one member's counts, not a full log.

In a TheRX discussion thread, a member warned that a website using his name and offering his plays for free was not his and that at the time he sold only through Pregame. Buyers should check where they are paying.

On Sportsbook Review, a member who said they had subscribed to the Las Vegas Advisor forum for five or six months wrote that anyone following his picks the year before was slaughtered, that he hit about 47% for a 30 unit loss, and that moderators deleted posts tallying his record. Another member in the thread said they had a yearly membership, saw him up about 12 units that season and planned to renew. We could not verify either account.

On the Las Vegas Advisor forum a member shared an outside tally putting his posted college and NFL plays at 127-142.5-3, minus 30.77 units on his own weighting, and said he would have done better following Fezzik's contest picks. The forum's administrator replied that he did not know whether the method was valid and that he had personally made money on the posted picks.

Other Las Vegas Advisor members were happier. In October 2009 one counted him 71-49 weighted since early September and another said his totals had saved them. In January 2010 a member listed his football futures at 16-4, though replies said some losing futures and bowl totals were not counted.

In a 2012 Las Vegas Advisor thread, one member called him an icon whose views they always consider, while another said he had been crushed over the past two years and that the forum existed mainly because people paid for his picks. A third said the record so far was pretty awful but they were staying on.
We found no reviews of his SIC Picks packages, no app store listing, and no Better Business Bureau or Trustpilot page for him. Our Reddit archive and library checks found only the 2025 comment above.

conflicts: The Sports Injury Central promotions page sends readers to prediction market apps (Kalshi, Polymarket, ProphetX and Novig) through tracked links, and offers a free week of its own picks product for signing up. That suggests SIC earns from referrals. It says nothing about Fezzik's picks, but it is a financial interest a buyer should know about.

His own website, stevefezzik.com, still says "Steve Fezzik's picks are only available at Pregame.com", while the SIC page says "Steve Fezzik Picks are only available for purchase here at SIC." Pregame still lists him in its pros menu. The older pages appear out of date; buy only through a page you can trace to him today.
The "3rd party" behind his "doubly documented" units is not named on the SIC page, so a buyer cannot check it.
strengths: A real, named bettor with contest wins that the contest organizers themselves publish, and newspaper accounts from 2006 and 2010.
His contest entries together beat contest lines in 2025: 55.3% across five Circa entries and 55.1% across four Westgate half season entries.
Prices and package contents are listed openly, with weekly options so a buyer can test before committing to a season.
He shares free material in public, such as NFL power ratings and a free weekly NFL pick at SIC, and SIC's own FAQ tells buyers to line shop and judge over at least a month.
When challenged in public he has answered, and in January 2026 he told unhappy buyers to buy someone else.
concerns: No full public log of his SIC picks. The unit totals in his marketing come from him and his sellers, and the "3rd party" is not named.
Unit totals for the same years differ from page to page: +241, +257 and just under 260 for 2020 to 2024.
Contest claims quote his best entry and leave out the others. In the 2026 SuperContest his two entries were 42-57-1 combined after Week 10.
SIC says purchases are non refundable, and no guarantee is offered on his packages.
Buyer posts alleging losing paid results recur from 2009 to 2026, though none includes a full log.
Discount codes and countdown offers push buyers to decide quickly.
checklist: Ask SIC for every Fezzik pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of contest wins is not a paid record.
Ask who the "3rd party" is that documents his units, and check it yourself.
Look up the current Westgate and Circa standings for the FEZZIK aliases before you pay; they are free PDFs on the organizers' sites.
Count units, not wins. Contest records ignore price; paid picks do not.
If you buy weekly, check your SIC account settings for automatic renewal.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Yes, he is a real Las Vegas bettor with contest wins reported by the Las Vegas Sun and shown on Westgate and Circa Sports standings. That proves contest success, not that his paid picks make money for buyers.
Is Steve Fezzik his real name?

No. A 2006 Los Angeles Times profile said Fezzik is a pen name he uses for safety, borrowed from the giant in The Princess Bride, and that he gave the paper his real name so his story could be confirmed.
Where can I buy Steve Fezzik's picks?

Since spring 2026, through SIC Picks at Sports Injury Central. He announced on 1 Apr 2026 that he was leaving Pregame.com after about 13 years. His own website and his old Pregame profile still point to Pregame, so check that you are on the SIC page.
How much does Steve Fezzik cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 SIC Picks sold his NFL picks or his college football picks for $79 a week or $799 a season each, and both together for $129 a week or $1,199 a season. SIC says purchases are non refundable.
Does Steve Fezzik have a verified record?

His contest results are published by the organizers, including a 2025 Westgate second half win and a tie for 9th in the 2025 Circa Million. His paid pick record is not: the unit totals come from him and his sellers and do not agree with each other, and no Watchdog graded record is matched to him.

For the money you get every NFL or college football play, or both, from a proven contest player, including futures and props, with email and SMS alerts. What is unproven is whether those paid picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over a large sample, and there is no refund if they do not.
